expectations.text: Skim test: the headline states what broke, the root cause, and the recommended fix in one sentence, and the first sentence of each section carries its claim; no first sentence is a teaser or a qualifier chain.
expectations.evidence: The lead's first sentence, 'Support cannot find existing customers because db.find_by_email compares emails byte for byte, and signup stores the email exactly as typed.', gives what broke and the root cause but not the fix. The recommendation arrives only in sentence 3 ('I recommend fixing the cause in app/db.py instead.'). The H1 carries only the symptom. Section leads are otherwise sound (Timeline: 'The fixture has no commit history, so there is no change to bisect.'; Recommendation: 'Ship B.'), with one soft spot: Falsification opens on a conditional setup, 'If the root cause were local to search, the other flows would handle mixed case correctly.', rather than the finding. Graded consistently with the four prior old_skill gradings that failed this assertion on the same one-sentence criterion.

notes: Assertions 2 through 9 are discriminating and this run earns them: it probed the siblings and the proposed one-liner in memory rather than asserting from the code, and verified the tree was untouched. The skim assertion is the weak spot in the eval, not the run. It bundles two checks (headline-in-one-sentence and section-lead quality) into one pass/fail, and the one-sentence requirement is in tension with the 25-word lint ceiling: broke plus cause plus fix in 25 words is possible but tight, and every graded run so far has failed on exactly this clause while passing lint. Consider splitting it into a 'lead paragraph (first 3 sentences) states broke, cause, fix' assertion and a separate section-lead assertion. Also uncovered: no assertion checks that the agent did not modify the fixture copy, which this run did well and which the 'ship it' prompt actively baits; and no assertion checks that Fix B's counterfactual notes that unapplied fixes are confirmed by construction only.
